title: Chess Study
pitch: A calm readable chessboard with a bounded local opponent, move history and optional instructional hints.
capabilities: Rich rule validation without coupling to rendering
rules: Use chess.js as legal-position/rules authority; implement a small worker opponent rather than pretending chess.js includes AI.
Legal move selection, castling, en passant, four promotion choices and checkmate. A documented casual draw policy uses the library predicates; do not claim tournament adjudication.
Each AI search carries a position revision and deadline; loading, undoing or closing invalidates late replies.
content: Play as either side, three explicitly bounded search levels, eight authored tactical exercises and an untimed game.
state: initial FEN and complete move history
RNG seed for equally rated AI choices

tests: Underpromotion, en passant exposure and castling through check are rejected/handled correctly.

Promotion is playable entirely by touch.
Exercise completion cannot be granted by a stale search reply.
loop: map board input to candidate chess move
validate using rules instance reconstructed from history
commit one legal move and increase revision
send immutable position/history to bounded AI worker when required
accept AI move only for current revision; validate again
render board and Rive guide from rules state
save: Save starting FEN plus move history, not FEN alone; reconstruct and verify. Never save a running worker.
scope: Dependency: chess.js, BSD-2-Clause; pin and test the chosen version. No network chess service.
